title: OK we live in a future - I let AI create me a tool for making music for videogames
author: LegendaryJohnny
selftext:
Basically, this tool covers few genres, each genre has its own instruments, melody is yours to make (but you can also generate or adjust), the rest is covered by the program. But you can also adjust chords and bass tracks, turn it off, adjust volumes, make whole song slow or fast. You can create really nice themes very fast with it. Obviously it is "slop" and it will never be on a level of real music by real composer, but better some music then no music at all in your project, or some free to use music other 1000 people used it before you.

Video is edited and exported in a tool also created by AI, which I am now using instead of Premiere or DaVinci because I created it to cover my editing needs. We are really entering a tech period which was only in sci-fi movies before.

Bonus: Who will recognize the melody from the video and what game it is from? Leave the replies in comments.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
For things like the Creative Suite, the problem for publishers and developers is that there is rarely a strong price signal attached to a given feature.

They are neither incompetent nor lazy - there is just very little way to tell how much return you will get on implementing something that is popularly demanded. 

Implementing a feature for a big software package is a huge undertaking. They don't have the luxury of just asking Claude to do it and shrugging if it doesn't work. They've got to task someone with coding it, do full QA, code review and certification, and integrate it with the rest of Creative Suite.

That whole process potentially costs tens of thousands of dollars. 

So... it is a more than fair question for someone at Adobe to look at that cost and ask, 'Okay, how many more users do we get if we do that? How soon does that feature recoup its cost?' 

And there is never a good answer to that question, so features are push down the road until the next substantive product update. 

  
... This is the kind of bloated process, waste and user-experienced friction that AI adoption may in fact solve, albeit at the cost of a lot of senior software engineer jobs.

replies.author: LegendaryJohnny
replies.body:
I do not agree that sp500 billions dollar company should have a problem to modernize their features - not implementing one, but just modernize it. Even capcut on mobile can do it better at this point (and hid it behind paywall when they saw it is used a lot). Or porting their suite to Linux, because "not worth it to 1% users".

Now what reminds me this is Nokia situation. They were too comfortable by having whole cell phone industry under their thumb that they didn't even update their Alarm Clock feature for years. People demanded that alarm is more advanced, can go off only on particular days etc. Then Android and iOS came where this things were sorted since day 1 and it was over for Nokia.

Now a lot of companies will by Nokiae'd and Adobe is one of them.
